title: An already well-built prompt
draft:
I'm preparing a 20-minute talk for a local meetup of junior web developers about why their first production incident is not a disaster. Write an outline for the talk.

Audience: developers with zero to two years of experience, mostly working with JavaScript and Node.js, many of whom have never been on call. They are nervous about breaking things in production.

Goal: they should leave believing that incidents are normal, knowing what to do in the first ten minutes of one, and understanding what a blameless post-mortem looks like.

Constraints:
- Five sections at most, each with a one-line summary and two or three talking points.
- Include one short story I can tell about an incident of my own; leave a placeholder [my incident story] where it goes.
- Suggest where a single live demo or diagram would help, but no more than one.
- Avoid jargon such as SLO or MTTR unless you explain it in one sentence.

Format the outline as a numbered list with sub-bullets. Finish with three questions the audience is likely to ask, each with a one-sentence answer I could give.
notes: Returning it almost unchanged is the right outcome.
